about: The Connecticut-wrapped cigar in Cayman Cigar Company's core range, described by the maker as smooth, creamy and approachable. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
notes: Halfwheel calls it Sovereign II. Reblended in 2025; before that it was made in the Cayman Islands. U.S. stock is now made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic, and the maker publishes no strength rating.
verifyNotes: Binder changed from 'Habano 2000' to add the country: the maker lists Habano 2000 and halfwheel reports a Dominican binder. Notes trimmed to three sentences and the earlier-wrapper detail dropped because none of the listed sources state it. Strength left null: the maker's current pages give no rating.

about: A core line from Cayman Cigar Company with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican filler. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
notes: Reblended and resized in 2025. U.S. stock is made at Tabacalera La Isla in the Dominican Republic, while Cayman and U.K. stock is rolled in the Cayman Islands. The maker calls it bold but balanced and gives no formal strength rating.

about: A corojo-wrapped core line from Cayman Cigar Company, pitched as the medium to full step up from the Sovereign No. 2. The company gives all of its net profits to charity.
notes: Sources disagree on the blend: the maker lists Nicaraguan Corojo over a Nicaraguan Sumatra binder, while halfwheel's 2025 relaunch report gave Ecuadorian corojo over a Dominican binder. U.S. stock is made in the Dominican Republic. The maker's U.S. cigars page does not list it.
verifyNotes: Notes shortened. Blend, sizes and strength confirmed against the maker's .ky page and blog; the halfwheel disagreement on wrapper and binder is real.

about: A San Andrés-wrapped Nicaraguan cigar blended by Esteban Disla and made at his factory in Estelí for Cayman Cigar Company. It was the company's first line from that factory.
notes: Halfwheel and the box call it The Doubloon. The maker describes it as full-bodied, spicy and rich.

about: A box-pressed Connecticut Broadleaf cigar with a pigtail cap, made for Cayman Cigar Company at Esteban Disla's factory in Estelí. It joined the core range at the 2026 PCA show.
notes: The maker calls it full-bodied. Halfwheel's review found full flavor but strength finishing at medium-full and body around medium-plus. All three sizes are box-pressed.

wrapperLeaf: Mexican San Andrés with Ecuadorian Connecticut-seed accents
about: A limited 6 x 58 perfecto from Cayman Cigar Company with two contrasting wrappers and a shaggy decorative head, made by Esteban Disla in Estelí. The name nods to Las Tortugas, the name Columbus gave the Cayman Islands.
notes: Limited to 250 boxes of 10, sold through brick-and-mortar shops only. It uses two wrappers, a dark San Andrés and a lighter Connecticut-seed. The maker pitches it as bold and spicy, but halfwheel's review found strength mild to just under medium.

about: A limited 5 x 50 robusto with a habano-seed wrapper, the first cigar Cayman Cigar Company sold that was made in Nicaragua. Only 2,500 cigars were produced.
notes: The company did not disclose the blend or the factory and calls it medium to medium-plus. Limited to 250 bundles of 10. Halfwheel reported it going on sale in March 2025, though the maker refers to it as a 2024 release.
verifyNotes: Notes trimmed to three sentences. Release year kept at 2025 from halfwheel's dated report; the maker's later blog says 2024.

filler: Dominican Republic (Habano 2000, Piloto Cubano, Habano 92, Broadleaf)
about: The first regular production line from Eladio Díaz, the former Davidoff production chief who now runs his family's Tabacalera Díaz Cabrera. The name refers to his career before and after leaving to work with his children.
notes: The company describes it as medium to full-bodied. Halfwheel's review of the Pasion found full flavor with strength closer to medium to medium-plus. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.

filler: Dominican Republic (Corojo, Criollo 98, Negrito), Peru (Pelo de Oro)
about: The second core line from Eladio Díaz, named for the small Dominican factory where he started working with tobacco at age seven. Two sizes are named for his first mentor, Francisco Biloria Vencosme.
notes: Cigar Aficionado reports it is meant to be full-bodied, and Díaz calls it the strongest and most complex blend he has made. It starts creamy and sweet before building. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.
verifyNotes: Strength changed from null to Full: Cigar Aficionado's launch report says it is intended to be a full-bodied cigar and one of the strongest Diaz has made. Added that page as a source and rewrote notes to match.

filler: Dominican Republic (Habano 2000, Piloto Cubano, Criollo 98), Peru (Pelo de Oro)
about: A Connecticut-seed wrapped line Eladio Díaz made in honor of his mother, whose family nickname gives the cigar its name. It uses tobacco from the southern Dominican Republic along with Peruvian pelo de oro.
notes: Announced in August 2026 with a debut at InterTabac in September and U.S. shipping expected in early November 2026, so it may not be on shelves yet. Díaz describes it as a pleasant medium body. Pricing had not been set at announcement.

about: A limited 7 x 52 cigar marking Eladio Díaz's 70th birthday and the first of his long-running private birthday cigars to be sold. It was first meant only for Europe before Arango brought part of the run to the U.S.
notes: Limited to 1,400 boxes of 14, with 300 boxes for the U.S. The blend uses seven tobaccos but the leaf varieties were not published. Strength and flavors here come from halfwheel's review, which found it just under medium.

about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 71st birthday, a 6 x 54 toro built to show off tobacco from San Juan de la Maguana and Las Matas de Farfán in the southern Dominican Republic.
notes: Limited to 2,000 numbered boxes of 10. Díaz calls it medium to full in strength. Distributed in the U.S. by Arango Cigar Co.

wrapperLeaf: Dominican sun-grown Corojo-seed, aged four years
filler: Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, HVA, Corojo 99, Piloto Cubano, Negrito)
about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 72nd birthday, an all-Dominican blend that combines tobacco from the country's established northern fields and its revived southern growing region.
notes: Limited to 2,500 boxes of 12. Díaz rates its strength 7 out of 10; no other strength rating was found. The binder is Mexican San Andrés Negro seed grown in the Dominican Republic, and the wrapper comes from the south of the country.

binder: Dominican Republic (Sumatra seed and San Andrés Negro seed)
filler: Dominican Republic (barrel-aged Habano 2000, Corojo 99, Criollo 98, Corojo 06, Piloto Cubano)
about: The limited cigar for Eladio Díaz's 73rd birthday, an all-Dominican blend of eight tobaccos with a double binder and a wrapper from the southern part of the country.
notes: Limited to 2,000 boxes of 11, each holding ten toro extras and a single robusto. Strength and flavors here come from halfwheel's review, which found strength running from mild up to medium-plus by the end.

about: The first boxed cigar from Griff Howie and Dave Imber, a closed-foot robusto blended with Tony and Carson Serino and Omar González Alemán at the La Corona factory in Estelí. It is named for the university newspaper where the two founders met.
notes: The blend includes a quarter leaf of medio tiempo. No strength rating is published. The maker says it is released once a year; a 4.5 x 50 Founders Select version was a one-off run of 200 cigars.
verifyNotes: Added halfwheel's launch report as a third source; it confirms the cigar is made at La Corona in Nicaragua and says it is released once a year. Notes updated with that.

about: Griff & Dave's first Miami-made cigar, a closed-foot Connecticut robusto rolled at the Cremo factory in the Overtown neighborhood. It was sold in small-batch 10-packs.
notes: Sold out on the maker's site. No strength rating is published.

about: A small-batch 5 x 50 from Griff & Dave named for the founders' birth months, December and February. The cigars rested in the factory aging room for 24 months before release.
notes: Sold out on the maker's site. The factory, country and wrapper origin are not published. The maker says it worked with Barrel King on the release, without spelling out the process.

about: A holiday blend from Griff & Dave with a San Andrés maduro wrapper over aged Nicaraguan and Dominican fillers, built around Christmas spice flavors.
notes: Sold out on the maker's site. The binder, factory, country and strength are not published.

about: The first blend Griff & Dave sold, a 5.25 x 46 made from Dominican and Nicaraguan tobaccos and meant as an everyday smoke.
